questions.text: What is a vacancy defect in a crystal lattice?
How does an interstitial defect differ from a vacancy defect?
What is a line dislocation and how does it affect the properties of a material?

answers.text: A vacancy defect occurs when an entire row of atoms is missing from its normal lattice site.
An interstitial defect involves single atoms or single-atom locations, which can alter the electrical properties differently than vacancy defects.
A line dislocation disrupts the normal geometric periodicity of the lattice and can alter the electrical properties of the material in a more unpredictable manner.
